problem: The minimum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)=3{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+3{x}_{3}^{2}-2{x}_{1}{x}_{3},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $1.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the minimum is attained?

activity_context.topic_title: Constrained Optimization of Quadratic Forms: Determining Where Extrema are Attained

examples.knowledge_point: Finding Where the Extrema of a Quadratic Form Are Attained on the Unit Sphere
examples.problem: The maximum value of the quadratic form $Q(\mathbf{x})= -x_1^2+2x_2^2+6x_3^2+4x_1x_2,$ when $\| \mathbf{x} \| = 1,$ is equal to $6.$ Find a vector $\mathbf{x}$ at which the maximum is attained.
examples.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(\mathbf{x}),$ when $\| \mathbf{x} \|=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A{:}$

$$
\max \{ Q(\mathbf{x}) \: | \:  \| \mathbf{x} \| = 1 \} = \lambda_{\textrm{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector $\mathbf{u}_{\textrm{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(\mathbf{x}),$ when $\| \mathbf{x} \|=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A{:}$

$$
\min \{ Q(\mathbf{x}) \: | \:  \| \mathbf{x} \| = 1 \} = \lambda_{\textrm{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector $\mathbf{u}_{\textrm{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14077353/assets/3449b02c92b2b2534241d33f7b6288d8433eb907b5a97ad255aa9fd5022d5971.png)

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda_{\textrm{max}}=6{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-6I & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 6\end{aligned}]-6[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-6I)\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ gives the eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14077353/assets/07bb866fbd14af52b5f3d01c91f6f58e1a7ef5bc4d70ada8c3a745035cae9e92.png)   

Since $\mathbf{v}$ is already normalized ($\|\mathbf{v}\|=1$), we conclude that,   ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14077353/assets/467bac248fa9988f4ee41bb9adaaf5e7ecbdf0e7e47b66a091ff5edf799e6799.png)

feedback.problem: The maximum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}-6{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $4.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the maximum is attained?
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=4:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-4I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -3 \\ -3 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-4I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{2},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
